lesson: On this task and loss, activity-memory networks of FW's size (the one-gate twin, a textbook GRU) do not learn to home from scratch at any tried learning rate (3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3) within 4,000 iterations; FW passes the 10 s stage by learning on 3 of 3 seeds.
evidence: sweeps.json; cold_summary.json; 0 of 12 rival cold runs passed any stage by learning

lesson: The homing loss (distance over the last 10 s of the return) rewards spinning on the spot: for a memoryless brain it roughly halves the loss relative to not steering, while making the score worse. This is a trap for any network without a working memory.
evidence: trap.json: 30 s, loss 11.5 never steers vs 6.6 spinning; score 4.57 vs 6.09

lesson: The rivals' failure is about the learning signal, not capacity: with a dense teacher (a linear readout charged for its home-vector error every wander tick, x0.1), both twin and GRU learn to home from scratch (best twin 1.94, best GRU 2.11 on the standard exam).
FW escapes the trap because its Hebbian board accumulates a tally from the first tick with no training, so gradient descent only has to learn to read it.
evidence: FW learns 10 s within ~250-900 iterations cold; activity nets need a teacher; not tested directly (e.g. FW with the board frozen at init)

lesson: Surgery (removing FW's board to make a warm twin) leaves the turn output at full lock, where tanh is flat and the gradient barely passes. Re-centring the turn bias gives a random-walk start, but the warm twins still slide back into spinning; even with the teacher, warm twins spin while cold twins with the teacher learn. FW's weights are a worse start for an activity memory than random weights.

A 30 s stop costs FW about 0.6 on the exam; teacher-trained activity networks pay 0.05 to 0.23. Inside FW, the home vector survives the stop (refitted readout error 0.8-1.1 vs 0.42-0.50 before) but the board shrinks (erase gate eases from ~0.0065 to ~0.0045 per tick while standing but never closes), so FW's fixed reading reads it short.
status: measured (mechanism for FW); activity nets' smaller cost despite more information lost is unexplained

lesson: Per-trip scores in the five-trip test rise for every brain including the random walk (later trips are harder). Compare against a baseline on the same trips before calling a reset partial.
evidence: random 4.10 -> 5.30; FW run 41 +0.18 trip 1 to trips 2-5; teacher twin +0.31 with a free wipe

lesson: The teacher term (reading the home vector from activity) does not help FW: run 41 1.49 -> 1.76, run 45 1.55 -> 1.59. FW keeps the vector on the board, not in activity.
The usual 200-trip exam (seed 4242) is about 0.06 kind compared with 1,000 fresh trips (seed 5151), for FW and rivals alike; orderings are unchanged.

Machine: 6 fast + 12 efficiency cores. One thread per run is as fast as four; about 13 simultaneous runs is comfortable; 20+ slows everything 2-3x; the macOS background policy throttles a process ~14x.

Round 3: matching the twin's starting setting to FW's (hold gate started almost shut, -5 or -3) and then matching FW's structure (32 fast + 32 slow neurons) did not let it learn: 0 of 18 rival runs homed better than not steering (best 4.86); FW from scratch with the same recipe scored 1.86, 5.23, 2.60. A one-population activity memory started slow cannot follow the heading, and training opens its gates (0.008 -> 0.23 by iteration 700).
evidence: charter3.md; results.json twinH_*, twinH3_*, twinS_*, gruH_*

lesson: The learned eraser fires at the start of each trip (first tick 0.84 with food, 0.75 without), not on arriving at food (0.005). It uses the world's free activity wipe at trip start as its cue. Earlier 'erase at food' descriptions are wrong in mechanism though right in effect in this world.
evidence: narrative 12:40; run 41 and run 19, 200 flies, food_stand 4 vs 0, arrival ticks

lesson: Round 4: FW learns even with its board empty at the start (write strength 0 -> ~0.03 within 50 iterations); the head-start contents are not the cause of FW's trainability, the one-knob distance to a working memory is. A twin handed a working counter learned on 1 of 3 starts; a trap-free grade (smooth closest approach + 0.2 x last-10 s) alone did not rescue the twin. The last-10-s grade has a measured valley (partial memories worse than spinning); closest approach does not.
status: measured, 3 starts per group, 10 s stage only

lesson: Round 5 (5 starts, stable steps): FW learns 3/5 with a full or an empty board (board switched on by iteration 30-40); plain twin 0/5; twin with a hand-built counter 2/5 and then as good as FW. Every failure still holds the way home. Rule of thumb: learnable from this grade iff a working memory is present or one knob away. Rejected: FW's edge is a built-in multiplication for reading (untrained FW and head-start twin encode the ideal turn equally).
status: measured, 5 starts per group, 10 s stage

lesson: Round 6 memory test (no steering, dense readout): learned keys and values with FW's lid and small write strength remembered best on every test (0.73 at 30 s vs FW 1.83; 6.6 vs 9.1 at 90 s) with 320 state numbers against FW's 4,160. The same design without the lid overflowed and learned nothing.

Every delta-rule memory (DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, Titans-style, delta on FW's board) path-integrates worse than the adding rules: the delta rule writes the surprise, and counting needs accumulation. A blend knob between Hebb and delta stays at Hebb.
A one-layer transformer with fixed sine positions trained on 30 s walks fails beyond 30 s (1.2 -> 6.9 at 40 s, 14.4 at 90 s; one start worse than knowing nothing).

Learnable from the homing score at 10 s: transformer 3/3, FW 3/5, FW+blend 1/3; every key-value table, delta form and Mamba 0/3. Separator (found after the results): how well untrained ACTIVITY encodes the home direction at 10 s - learners 0.76-0.83, all failures <= 0.63. Consistent with round 5's 'memory present or one knob away'. The pre-registered forecast from the store's R^2 failed; that probe is unreliable for 256-cell tables (ridge-dependent).

No new knob (direct read, per-neuron forget, blend) beat 800 more iterations of plain practice on trained FW; the practice itself gave the project's best network (run 45 retrained: 1.35 standard, 1.444 on 1,000 fresh trips).

A memory must be within reach early in training to be learned from the final score: across 54 runs of rounds 5-6, runs whose activity pointed home (R^2 >= 0.7 at iteration 0, 100 or 200) learned 12 of 24; the rest 0 of 30. Within reach is necessary, not sufficient (the lid hybrid gets there and still spins). 'One knob away' shows up as reaching it by iteration 100 (FW with an empty board).
status: measured; measure and threshold chosen after the results

lesson: After round 6: a memory close to working raises the chance of learning from the final score (0/20 below early R^2 0.4, ~40% above 0.7, 96 runs) and lowering it on purpose lowers learning (transformer attention sharpening: 5/5 -> 2/4, score 1.65 -> 2.53); but it does not decide the outcome. Every run first learns to turn hard; learners are those that ease off later. The loss landscape at birth (steer vs spin slopes) does not predict who learns. Twin with 4 or 8 counters (birth 0.83) learned 0/8 vs 16 counters 3/9.
status: measured; 4-9 tries per setting; predictions partly failed
evidence: charter6.md results 21:00; dial_results.json, slope.json, race.json, reach.json
